title: Open House: a PSX-style zombie siege, with destructible environment
author: ToddAwl
selftext:
Hey guys,

I've been making a co-op zombie game called Open House (working title) with Claude Code and wanted to share where it's at. It's very early and I'm not experienced at all with this. The video is mostly me shooting, with a bit of barricading.

The idea: you and up to 4 friends are stuck in a six-floor "smart home" that's secretly a test site for infected. You barricade a floor, hold it for a wave, then fall back up to the next one, all the way to the roof. PS1 look, made in Godot 4.

Fair warning, the first-person hands and guns look pretty bad right now. The grips, the trigger finger, the reloads.

What's in so far:

Zombies that use the house. They push furniture together, climb over stuff, give each other leg-ups, stack crates under windows, and remember which ways in worked against you last game

Special zombies: a bruiser who smashes through walls, a screamer who calls more in, wall climbers and crawlers, another one I'm working on is a tether, basically a zombie abomination with a really long tongue that uses it to make zombies climb faster to higher floors.

Eventually it will be a 4 player coop at the moment testing with 2-player co-op with voice chat (Mac and Linux (Steamdeck)) just because that what I have lol. If you die you can watch the house cameras and mark zombies for your friend

Boarding up windows and doorways, dragging furniture against doors

A few things to mess about with in the house, like darts and a basketball hoop

Most of the effort has gone into testing, because physics zombies break in weird ways: there are about 100 automated test scenarios, bots that play waves and report stuck zombies, and an in-game view that shows what each zombie is thinking.

Working on a lot at the moment: zombies tackling barricades as a group, smoother animation, better first-person arms (need some tips for that one haha), and a pile of bugs the bots keep finding.

Would love feedback, especially if you've done physics-heavy AI or phone mocap, first person arms etc.
